page: Amazon Web Services r8i.metal-48xl is a memory-optimized bare-metal server powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. It is equipped with 1536.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations.

In benchmark evaluations, the r8i.metal-48xl demonstrates top-tier performance, particularly in multi-core and memory-intensive operations. Multi-core CPU benchmarks, such as stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests, place the server in the top 10% of all tested configurations. Its memory subsystem achieves top-tier read and write bandwidth, with cached read bandwidth reaching 15490.0 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 585.17 GB/sec. Additionally, the platform excels in database operations, showing top-tier results in Passmark database tests and Redis SET operations, alongside high static web serving throughput.

While the server lacks local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware, it compensates with a baseline network bandwidth of 75 Gbps. The absence of local storage means workloads must rely on network-attached storage options. Qualitatively, the server represents a high-density resource profile suitable for enterprise-scale workloads that demand massive memory footprints and high parallel processing capabilities without requiring local disk I/O. It is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, heavy virtualization, software compilation, and CPU-based machine learning inference, where its AMX instructions deliver top-tier prompt processing speeds.
